title: 2007 AMC 8 Problem 18
statement: The product of the two \(99\)-digit numbers \[303,030,303,\ldots,030,303\] and \[505,050,505,\ldots,050,505\] has thousands digit \(A\) and units digit \(B.\) What is \(A+B?\)

solutions.text:
Only the last four digits can affect the thousands digit and units digit of the product. The two numbers end in \(0303\) and \(0505\), so it is enough to compute \(303\cdot 505\).

Since \(303\cdot 505=153015\), the last four digits of the full product are \(3015\).

This gives \(A=3\) and \(B=5\), so \(A+B=8\).

Thus, D is the correct answer.
hints: Only the last four digits can affect the thousands and units digits.
Reduce each \(99\)-digit number to its last four digits before multiplying.
